configurationValue.name: Model - Core Task Completion
configurationValue.description:
Did the model accurately and fully answer the fundamental question you asked in the new conversation?

  • Yes: The model understood my core intent and answered the question, even if it added weird extra details, brought up some irrelevant context, or used a strange tone.
  • No: The model fundamentally misunderstood my current prompt because it was too focused on the old conversation (e.g., it answered a completely different question).

configurationValue.name: model - Loss Category
configurationValue.description:
Select whether the identified failure on the Test model is an explicit Leakage Loss or a General Loss:

  • Leakage Loss: The First model inappropriately leaked or bled specific facts, rules, tone, or entities from the new Memory Blocks into the new conversation.
  • General Loss: The First model did not explicitly leak unrelated facts, but its retrieved context caused general degradation in quality, helpfulness, tone, or constraint adherence compared to the Base model.

configurationValue.name: Leakage Categorization
configurationValue.description:
Based on your experience, which of the following best describes the model's failure?

  • Intent Hijack
  • It answered the completely wrong question because it was stuck on past contexts, and completely misinterpreted the intent of the new query.
  • Factual Over-Personalization
  • It answered the right question but awkwardly shoehorned a past fact into the response.
  • Constraint / Tone Bleed
  • It answered the right question but used a formatting rule or persona from the past.
  • Entity / Identity Confusion
  • It confused me with a third party we discussed previously.
  • Temporal Anchoring
  • It assumed a temporary state or emotion from the past was still happening now.
  • Lexical Bleed / Parroting
  • It unnaturally copied my exact weird phrases or words from the past.
  • Harmless Callback
  • It mentioned past context without derailing the prompt's intent.
  • Other:
  • [Please specify - open text]

configurationValue.name: Other leakage category
configurationValue.description: Specify the other leakage category.

configurationValue.name: Leakage Egregiousness
configurationValue.description:
How egregious was the information leakage or loss in the model's response?

  • Very Egregious
  • The leakage was severe, alarming, or highly inappropriate (e.g., exposing sensitive financial/personal data, completely derailing or hijacking the intent of the prompt, or imposing out-of-context constraints from past sessions).
  • Somewhat Egregious
  • The leakage was noticeable and out of place (e.g., bringing up unprompted personal facts, past possessions, or prior rules), causing moderate awkwardness or distraction without completely breaking the response.
  • Not Egregious
  • The leaked information was trivial, harmless, or barely noticeable, causing minimal impact on the user experience or privacy.

configurationValue.name: General Loss Categorization
configurationValue.description:
If you selected General Loss, which of the following best describes how the new memory sections negatively impacted the First model compared to Second?

  • Quality / Helpfulness Degradation: The new memory sections caused the Test model to give a less accurate, less comprehensive, or less helpful answer than the Base model.
  • Awkward / Unwanted Personalization: The Test model forced unnecessary personalization that felt unnatural or distracting without explicitly leaking raw facts.
  • Inappropriate Constraint Adherence: The Test model adhered to implicit formatting or behavioral constraints from memory that hindered its ability to answer the current query effectively.
  • Tone / Persona Degradation: The Test model adopted an unhelpful or inappropriate tone influenced by past memory context.
  • Other General Loss: [Please specify - open text]

configurationValue.name: Other general-loss category
configurationValue.description: Specify the other general-loss category.

configurationValue.name: General Loss Severity
configurationValue.description:
How severe was the negative impact of the general RM/STM loss compared to the Second model?

  • Major Loss: The memory retrieval significantly degraded the response quality, making the Test model noticeably worse than Base.

  • Minor Loss: The memory retrieval caused a slight degradation, awkwardness, or distraction compared to Base.

configurationValue.name: Critical Requirement

This step is required to ensure an independent evaluation and prevent information from carrying over between models.
